title: Type Conversion: Making Data Play Nice 🔄
description: Convert between strings, numbers, and more – because input is rarely perfect.

slides.title: When Worlds Collide
slides.content:
# You Can't Add Strings and Integers

```python
"Port: " + 80   # TypeError!
```
Python needs explicit conversion. That's where `int()`, `str()`, `float()`, and `bool()` come in. They create new objects of the target type.

slides.title: str() – Anything to String
slides.content:
# Convert Numbers to Text

```python
port = 80
message = "Port: " + str(port)
print(message)  # Port: 80
```
Also works on floats and booleans.

slides.title: str() Demo
slides.codeSnippet:
target = "192.168.1.1"
port = 8080
result = target + ":" + str(port)
print(result)

quizData.question: What does `str(3.14)` return?
quizData.explanation: str() converts the float to its string representation.

slides.title: int() – String to Integer
slides.content:
# Extract Numbers from Text

```python
port_str = "8080"
port_num = int(port_str)
print(port_num + 1)  # 8081
```
The string must look like a valid integer, else `ValueError`.

Also works with floats (truncates decimal): `int(9.9)` → `9`.

quizData.question: What is the result of `int("100", 2)`?
quizData.explanation: Interpreting the string '100' as base 2 (binary) yields 4 in decimal.

slides.title: float() – String to Float
slides.content:
# When You Need Decimals

```python
version = float("3.11")
print(version + 0.01)  # 3.12
```
Works similarly to int(), but accepts a decimal point.

slides.title: float() Parsing
slides.codeSnippet:
timeout_str = "2.5"
timeout_sec = float(timeout_str)
print(f"Timeout set to {timeout_sec}s")

quizData.question: `float("3.14.15")` will produce 3.14.
quizData.explanation: That string has two dots, causing a ValueError.

slides.title: bool() – Truthiness to Boolean
slides.content:
# Convert Any Value to True/False

```python
print(bool(1))        # True
print(bool(0))        # False
print(bool(""))       # False
print(bool("hack"))   # True
```
Useful when you want to explicitly test emptiness.

slides.content:
## Use `.isdigit()` to Check First

Strings have a method `.isdigit()` that returns True if all characters are digits. It helps avoid conversion errors.
